# PDF · Protein Database of Functionality

> Database of food protein functional properties extracted from published journal articles. Each value of 17 properties (solubility, emulsifying, foaming, gelling, water/oil holding, particle size, ζ-potential, PDI, sulfhydryl, disulfide, surface hydrophobicity, turbidity, degree of hydrolysis, free amino groups, encapsulation, antioxidant activity) is linked to a sample (protein source, composition, ingredients), its sample treatment and the test method. Data licence CC BY 4.0. Built by the AI4FH Lab, University College Dublin.

This file is for AI agents and scripts. The website (index.html) needs JavaScript and shows nothing to a plain HTTP fetch; all data are static files listed below. No sign-up, no API key.

Site root: https://dzjxzyd.github.io/Protein-Database_Functionality/ (all paths below are relative to it)
Source repository: https://github.com/dzjxzyd/Protein-Database_Functionality

## Entry point

- `data/download/manifest.json`: `release` (version, date, release notes), `built`, `files` (8 relational tables) and `props` (17 flat tables). Each entry has `path`, `rows`, `cols`, `bytes` and `sha256`. Check `sha256` after downloading; download again when `release.version` changes.

## Which file to use

- One property, everything in each row: `data/download/flat_<property>.csv.zip`, property = solubility, emulsifying, foaming, gelling, water_holding, oil_holding, particle_size, zeta_potential, pdi, sulfhydryl, disulfide, surface_hydrophobicity, turbidity, degree_of_hydrolysis, free_amino, encapsulation, antioxidant. One row per value, 61 columns (sample, ingredients, treatment, conditions, test method, paper).
- Whole database, joined yourself: `data/download/<table>.csv.zip` for papers, samples, ingredients, treatments, treatment_params, measurements, measurement_conditions, methods. Keys: `doi` → `sample_id` (`doi#N`) → `measurement_id`. A value's test method is the row of `methods.csv` with the same `doi` and `method_id`.

## Rules for reading the data

- Each zip holds one UTF-8 CSV with BOM plus README.md and LICENSE-DATA.md. pandas cannot read the zip directly (more than one file inside); open the CSV with zipfile.
- Compare across papers with `value_std` + `unit_std` (standard unit per property; empty when not convertible). `value` is in the article's unit (`unit`). If `multiplier` is not empty (e.g. 10^3), `value` is the axis reading and must be multiplied by it. Non-numeric entries (e.g. "<0.1") are in `value_text`.
- `data_origin` contains `model-derived` for values a model read from figures (estimates; `source_item` names the figure, `series` and `x` locate the point) and `author-reported` for values from the authors' tables or text. About 64% of values are model-derived.
- `significance` holds the authors' significance letters (a, b, ab …). They compare samples only within the same table or figure of the same paper (values sharing a letter are not significantly different). Never compare letters across papers.
- `sd` is the standard deviation as reported; `err_low` / `err_high` are the ends of an asymmetric error bar where one was given.
- Measurement conditions (pH, temperature, concentration, time …) are in `conditions_all` and the `cond_*` columns; they are not the sample treatment. Sample treatment (heating, ultrasound, hydrolysis …) is in `treatment_summary`, `treatment_types` and `treatments.csv`.
- `measure_name` is the paper's own label for the measurement (e.g. EAI, ESI, WHC). Some table-derived labels end with a footnote letter from the table header (e.g. "WAIc" = WAI with footnote c).
- Category columns are in Chinese. For English use `property`, `protein_source_std`, `protein_form_std`, `treatment_types`, `treatment_type`, `test_method_en` and `method_summary`. Several values in one cell are separated by " | ".
- No sentences from the articles are included. Report the DOI (https://doi.org/<doi>) with every number, label model-derived values as estimates, and tell the user to check important numbers against the article.

## Python example

```python
import io, zipfile, urllib.request
import pandas as pd

BASE = 'https://dzjxzyd.github.io/Protein-Database_Functionality/data/download/'
raw = urllib.request.urlopen(BASE + 'flat_solubility.csv.zip').read()
z = zipfile.ZipFile(io.BytesIO(raw))
df = pd.read_csv(z.open('flat_solubility.csv'), encoding='utf-8-sig', low_memory=False)
df['is_model'] = df['data_origin'].str.contains('model-derived')
soy = df[df['protein_source_std'].str.contains('Soybean', na=False)]
print(soy.groupby('unit_std')['value_std'].describe())
```
